tasks.short: Design assessments and judge learning outcomes from the results.

steps.what: Draft assessment items from learning outcome statements.

loop.input: Outcome statements and the last cohort's item list
loop.output: Draft items with the outcome id on each item
loop.check: Administrator checks each item against the outcome statement
loop.stop: One pass, at most 40 items. Blank items stay for the administrator. No second pass.
loop.why_not_simpler: Outcome statements are prose, so a fixed item bank cannot start a new outcome

steps.what: Agree the assessment with faculty before use.
Publish the agreed assessment in the learning system.
Administer the assessment sitting for this cohort.
Build the learning outcome score table.
Judge which learning outcomes are weak.

tasks.design: The {LMS} stores outcome statements, items and cohort scores, and a {BI} view builds the score table. A bounded pass drafts items from the statements; faculty agree the assessment before a sitting. The administrator writes which learning outcomes are weak, and that note is the only version that is kept.
tasks.previous_blocker: Items and scores sat in separate documents, and a weak outcome was a matter of reading, not a rule.
tasks.enabler_now: The learning system can export scores by outcome id, and a bounded pass can draft items for a person to check.
tasks.still_hard: Judging what a weak pattern means for the programme, and keeping faculty agreement when a statement changes.
tasks.human_edge: The administrator, with faculty, decides whether an outcome is weak. A score table does not make that call.

ambition.what: A programme-level outcome judgement at the end of each teaching period, not only when accreditation is due.

tasks.altitude: Item drafts and the score table are ready before the faculty meeting. The week still has the sitting and the judgement. The administrator can refuse an outcome claim the table does not support.

reach.task: Design a classroom test and read the results
reach.learn: Which outcome statements stay stable enough to reuse next term

evidence.claim: Naming a weak learning outcome is a professional judgement, not a cut-score rule.
AI Act Annex III 3(a) and 3(b) cover admissions and decisions on learning outcomes, so a person has to decide.
GDPR Article 22 requires human intervention where a decision about a person rests on automation alone.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: this task ends when the outcome judgement is recorded. It does not change a mark a teacher already gave.

Structured fields: programme id, outcome id, item id, cohort id, score. Faculty produce the score. If the export has no outcome id, the administrator types cohort totals and does not auto-fill the judgement.
Use the learning system's own item bank and grade export before any custom job. A scheduled extract is only for a gap the export cannot fill.
Native configuration is tested first. Custom code is not the starting point.
unknowns: Whether outcome statements already have stable ids in the learning system.
Who is allowed to record an official outcome judgement.
Whether students must be told how the outcome judgement is used.
research_questions: Which programmes lack an outcome id on the score export?
Does the learning system already store items against outcomes?

already_counted.description: Outcome judgement against the score table

incremental.description: Map new outcome ids and retire items that no longer match a statement

approvals.approved_version: outcome judgement note the administrator signed against the score table

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: faculty rewrite the items and the sitting is unchanged. High: the item bank is reused and the score table is only checked. The sitting and the judgement stay. Not a measured saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recruit, hire, train and sometimes terminate departmental personnel.

steps.what: Confirm the departmental personnel need with the chair.
Draft the vacancy and the selection criteria.

loop.input: Vacancy brief and the last agreed post template
loop.check: Administrator deletes any criterion that is not in the brief
loop.stop: One draft. If the brief lacks a pay band or a reporting line, the draft stops and those fields stay empty.
loop.why_not_simpler: The brief is a short note, not a form with every clause

steps.what: Screen applications for the departmental personnel post.

loop.input: Application packs and the agreed criteria
loop.output: A pass or gap flag per criterion, with the source line
loop.check: Administrator opens every flag against the application, not the summary
loop.stop: One pass per application. A missing document is a gap, not a rejection. No ranking score.
loop.why_not_simpler: Applications mix a form with a free-text letter a fixed field map misses

steps.what: Interview shortlisted applicants for the post.
Decide whether to hire or to terminate.
Send the approved offer or termination letter.
Train the new departmental hire on local routines.

tasks.design: The {ATS} holds the vacancy, the applications and the decision. A bounded pass drafts the vacancy from the brief and flags each application against the agreed criteria, with no ranking score. The offer or termination letter leaves {EMAIL} only from the decision the administrator recorded. Interviews and training stay in the room.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applications and termination cases were read one by one, and the letter was retyped from notes.
tasks.enabler_now: The recruitment system already stores applications, and a bounded pass can flag a criterion without choosing the person.
tasks.still_hard: The interview, the decision to hire or terminate, and training a new colleague.
tasks.human_edge: Only the administrator can hire, reject or terminate. Screening flags are not a decision.

ambition.what: Whether a vacancy brief is complete enough to open applications, in the same week the chair asks.

tasks.altitude: Shortlisting prep is shorter. The week still has interviews and training. The administrator can stop a letter that does not match the recorded decision.

reach.learn: Which selection criteria must stay with the interviewer and which can be checked from the file

evidence.claim: GDPR Article 22 names staff decisions among those that must not rest on automation alone.
AI Act Annex III 4(a) and 4(b) cover hiring and evaluating staff.
WOR article 27 requires works-council consent for staff-data arrangements in the Netherlands; other countries differ.
An interview and the decision to end employment are not a document check.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: from a confirmed vacancy or a termination case through the letter and, for a hire, the first local training. Payroll setup is out of scope.

Structured fields: post id, criterion id, application id, decision (hire, reject, terminate), letter template id. The chair produces the vacancy brief. If a criterion has no id, that application is read in full by the administrator.
Use the recruitment system's own vacancy and stage settings before a custom screen. No custom code until that cannot store the criteria.
Where national rules require works-council consent for staff data, the shortlist does not go live until that consent is in place.
unknowns: Who may sign a termination, and above which grade.
Whether the works council must consent before this recruitment workflow changes.
Which letter templates are already approved.
research_questions: Are selection criteria stored as fields today, or only inside the vacancy text?
Who is the delegated signer for a termination?

incremental.description: Keep post templates and criterion lists current after each hiring round

approvals.approved_version: hire or termination decision recorded in the meeting
offer or termination letter generated from that decision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most posts are unusual, so screening fails and interviews take the time. High: standard posts, a short check of flags, and the same interviews and training. The decision stays with the administrator. Not a measured saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct support staff and evaluate how their work goes.

steps.what: Read observed results of support staff work.
Direct support staff activities for the week.
Draft performance notes from the observed results.

loop.input: Week priorities and the load table
loop.output: Performance notes with each claim tied to a row or a meeting note
loop.check: Administrator removes any sentence that has no source row
loop.stop: One draft per person. A week with no note produces an empty note, not a guessed rating.
loop.why_not_simpler: The week's work is free text plus a table, and the note must follow both

steps.what: Evaluate staff performance and record the rating.

tasks.design: A {BI} view on {HCM} shows absence and workload before the weekly meeting. A bounded pass drafts performance notes only from that table and the meeting record. The rating is entered in {TALENT} by the administrator after the conversation, and no rating is written without that conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Load was copied into a side sheet, and the rating was written from memory after the meeting.
tasks.enabler_now: Absence and workload are already in the staff system, so the meeting can start from a view rather than a rebuild.
tasks.still_hard: Directing the week and judging a person's performance in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The rating is the administrator's judgement after talking to the person. Notes do not set it.
tasks.altitude: The weekly meeting and the rating conversation stay. The load table is ready beforehand. The administrator still decides the rating and can leave it blank.

reach.learn: Which absence figures are safe to show a manager before a one-to-one

evidence.claim: AI Act Annex III 4(a) and 4(b) cover evaluating staff.
WOR article 27 covers staff-data arrangements and needs works-council consent where that national rule applies.
Week-to-week direction of a team is a conversation, not a report.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: weekly direction of support staff and the performance rating that follows. Hiring and pay are separate tasks.

Structured fields: staff id, absence hours, workload category, week id, rating code. The staff system produces absence. If workload is not coded, the administrator does not invent a rating from the absence figure alone.
Use the staff system's own absence view and the talent system's rating form before any custom extract.
Staff-data views that are new need works-council consent where national rules require it. Until then the administrator keeps the current pack.
The performance draft uses observed results of the work. Planned priorities and absence figures do not stand in for those results.
unknowns: Whether workload categories exist or only job titles.
Who else must sign a rating before it is final.
Whether the works council has already consented to this staff view.
research_questions: Is workload recorded as hours by category, or only as a roster?

incremental.description: Fix workload categories when a support role changes

approvals.approved_version: performance rating recorded after the conversation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the week is the meeting and the rating conversation, and notes are rewritten. High: the load table is trusted and notes are edited, not rewritten. Direction and the rating stay. Not a measured saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise students on courses, graduation progress and careers.

steps.what: Open student records for progress toward graduation.
Compare completed courses with graduation rules.
Advise the student on course selection and career.
Send the checked study plan to the student.

loop.input: Advice notes and the rule check
loop.output: Study plan listing courses, exceptions and the career point discussed
loop.check: Administrator edits every course and exception before send
loop.stop: One draft. A course that is not in the notes or the rule check is dropped.
loop.why_not_simpler: The plan must follow what was said, which is not a form

steps.what: Log the study plan on the student record.

tasks.design: Student records and {LMS} results produce a rule check against the published graduation rules before the meeting. The advising conversation stays in person. A bounded pass drafts the study plan from the notes, and it is sent and filed only after the administrator edits it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress was rebuilt by hand before each meeting, and the plan was a mail written afterwards from memory.
tasks.enabler_now: Completed courses and published rules can be compared by code when both use the same course id.
tasks.still_hard: The conversation about course selection and a career, especially where the student's situation is not in the record.
tasks.human_edge: The advice is the administrator's. The rule check only shows what the published rules say.

ambition.what: Evening students who cannot attend drop-in hours get a written study plan in the same week as the conversation.

tasks.altitude: The meeting is unchanged. The rule check and a draft plan are ready. The administrator can withhold a plan that does not match what was said.

reach.role: Education and Childcare Administrators, Preschool and Daycare
reach.task: Advise a parent on a child's next step
reach.learn: Which rules can be checked before the conversation and which have to be heard from the person

evidence.claim: Course advice against a published rule is a conversation; the rule check is not the advice.
GDPR Article 22 requires a person where an automated result would decide about a student.
AI Act Annex III 3(b) covers systems that determine learning outcomes or access to education.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one advising case from the progress extract through the filed study plan. Teaching the course is a different task.

Structured fields: student id, programme version, course id, status (passed, enrolled, missing), rule id. The student-records system produces completions. If a course id does not match a rule, the row is listed as unresolved and the administrator decides it in the meeting.
The step text's student records system is the institution's student information system, not a new product.
Test the learning system's degree-audit or rule view before building a comparison. If it already shows missing courses, use that and skip the custom check.
unknowns: Whether a degree audit already exists and who trusts it.
Which career notes may be stored on the student record.
Whether evening students are in the same record as full-time students.
research_questions: Does the current degree audit match the published programme version?
Who may send an official study plan?

incremental.description: Update programme-rule rows when a curriculum version changes

approvals.approved_version: study plan the administrator edited before sending
study plan the administrator edited before sending

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most students have exceptions, so the rule check is thin and the meeting is the task. High: standard programmes, a short edit of the plan, and the same conversation. The advice is not automated. Not a measured saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Less of the week goes to blank forms, vacancy text and progress sheets. Interviews, supervision, sittings and advising stay. Hiring, ratings, outcome judgements and advice to a student remain the administrator's to sign.
reach: Kindergarten through secondary administrators can reuse the outcome-table check, not the university rules
Social and community service managers can see which hiring criteria belong in the interview
skills_to_grow: Reading a score table before signing an outcome judgement
Checking a vacancy brief is complete before applications open
Walking a student through a rule check without treating it as the advice
role.ambitious_version: Each programme has an outcome judgement for the period, each vacancy is complete before interviews, and each advising meeting starts from a rule check the student can see.
